review: The Arabic splits the first sentence across lines 1–2 (أَظْـ / ـهَرْتَ) because of a long word; Hebrew cannot split a word, so the sentence runs straight through 1:1–1:2.
1:4 כַּמְּנֹרָה — 'like the lampstand'; the Arabic كَالْمَنَار is a beacon, but מְנוֹרָה is the biblical lamp (Ex 25:31) and the light image survives.
3:3–3:4 יִוָּתֵר אַחֲרֵי הֶעָנָן / אַהֲבָתְךָ זוֹהֶרֶת — the Arabic has 'there remains after the cloud Your love, radiant'; Hebrew fronts the verb so the caesura falls in the same place as the tune.

4:5–4:6 לַמְּדֵנִי לְמַהֵר / לָשׁוּב אֵלֶיךָ מַהֵר — the Arabic repeats 'hasten' only once (أُسْرِعُ الْخُطْوَ رُجُوعًا); the repetition is added so the couplet rhymes and the tune has two equal halves.
